patterns.title: Clear user need and use cases
patterns.summary: The proposal should identify concrete users, use cases, and why the Web Platform is the right layer.
review_questions: What user need does the feature serve?
Why is a web-platform solution needed instead of an application convention?
evidence_requirements: explainer problem statement or specification introduction

patterns.title: Reuse existing platform primitives
patterns.summary: New behavior should integrate with existing primitives before introducing parallel concepts.
review_questions: Can existing events, promises, permissions, Fetch, URL, or policy mechanisms represent this behavior?

patterns.title: WebIDL and JavaScript consistency
patterns.summary: WebIDL APIs should follow platform conventions for objects, dictionaries, promises, exceptions, and exposure.
review_questions: Do IDL types, defaults, exceptions, and promise behavior match platform conventions?
common_mitigations: replace ad hoc callbacks with promises

patterns.title: Naming and type design
patterns.summary: Names, enum values, option dictionaries, and units should be clear, stable, and compatible with future extension.
review_questions: Are names precise, non-misleading, and extensible?
Are units and default values explicit?

patterns.title: Asynchronous operation and Promise behavior
patterns.summary: Operations that involve I/O, permission, storage, devices, crypto, or network work should have clear asynchronous behavior.
review_questions: When does the promise resolve or reject?
Can callers observe partial completion or retries?
common_mitigations: specify task source and rejection reasons

patterns.title: Cancellation and AbortSignal
patterns.summary: Long-running or externally mediated operations should define cancellation semantics and AbortSignal integration when appropriate.
review_questions: Can the caller cancel?
What happens to prompts, streams, and side effects after abort?

patterns.title: Error semantics
patterns.summary: Error states should be specific enough for recovery but not expose unnecessary private or security-sensitive detail.
review_questions: Are error names and timing defined?
Could errors become account, device, or permission oracles?

patterns.title: Feature detection and progressive enhancement
patterns.summary: Authors should be able to detect and use the feature progressively without brittle UA sniffing.
review_questions: How do authors detect support?
Does detection itself reveal high-entropy information?

patterns.title: Window and Worker exposure
patterns.summary: Exposure on Window, worker globals, service workers, or background contexts should match capability and lifecycle constraints.
review_questions: Which globals expose the feature?
Are background or service worker uses justified?
evidence_requirements: WebIDL exposure annotations and lifecycle text

patterns.title: Secure-context requirement
patterns.summary: Powerful or sensitive features should clearly state whether secure contexts are required.
review_questions: Is the feature restricted to secure contexts?
Is mixed-content or insecure-origin behavior defined?
evidence_requirements: secure context requirement in conformance text or IDL

patterns.title: User activation and expression of intent
patterns.summary: Features that expose capabilities, private data, or disruptive UI should bind use to a clear user gesture or chooser.
review_questions: What user action expresses intent?
Can embedded or background contexts trigger the feature without a gesture?
evidence_requirements: activation, prompt, or chooser processing model

patterns.title: Active-document lifecycle and BFCache behavior
patterns.summary: The feature should define behavior across navigation, page visibility, active documents, and BFCache transitions.
review_questions: What happens on navigation, page hide, restore, and discard?
Does state leak across lifecycle transitions?
common_mitigations: stop sensitive activity on page hide

patterns.title: Selection instead of unnecessary enumeration
patterns.summary: APIs should prefer user-mediated selection over exposing complete lists of devices, accounts, or local resources.
review_questions: Can the design return only the user-selected item?
Is enumeration needed before user intent?

patterns.title: Accessibility and internationalization defaults
patterns.summary: UI, rendering, text, and locale-sensitive behavior should preserve accessibility and internationalization expectations by default.
review_questions: How does the feature expose semantics to assistive technology?
Are direction, locale, and user preferences respected?

patterns.title: URL, Fetch, and HTTP integration
patterns.summary: Network-related behavior should integrate cleanly with URL parsing, Fetch, redirects, headers, caching, and service workers.
review_questions: How does the feature interact with Fetch, redirects, caches, and service workers?

patterns.title: Extensibility and forward compatibility
patterns.summary: The design should allow compatible evolution without parser breaks, hard-coded enumerations, or unversioned assumptions.
review_questions: How are unknown fields, versions, and extensions handled?
Can future values be added compatibly?

patterns.title: Safe defaults
patterns.summary: Default behavior should minimize privilege, exposure, persistence, and compatibility risk.
review_questions: What happens by default before author or user configuration?
Is the least powerful behavior the default?
common_mitigations: change default to deny or ephemeral

patterns.title: Rendering platform integration
patterns.summary: Rendering features should integrate with layout, painting, accessibility, user preferences, and progressive enhancement.
review_questions: How does the feature interact with layout, painting, accessibility, and user preferences?
common_mitigations: respect reduced motion or contrast preferences

patterns.title: Review package readiness
patterns.summary: Horizontal review requests should provide the reviewed snapshot, explainer or use cases, changed scope, self-review links, issue venue, and requested deadline.
review_questions: Is the exact reviewed snapshot clear?
Are self-review answers, changes since prior review, issue venue, and deadline available?
common_mitigations: add dated snapshot and self-review links
state scope and changes since prior review
evidence_requirements: review request issue, explainer, self-review, and status or transition request

patterns.title: Conceptual model and terminology clarity
patterns.summary: Specifications with abstract models, vocabularies, or layered APIs should explain core concepts, terms, abbreviations, and relationships for technically informed readers.
review_questions: Can an unfamiliar technical reader understand the core model from the abstract or introduction?
Are defined terms, abbreviations, and relationships introduced before use?
expected_properties: examples that connect model and syntax
common_mitigations: add examples linking concepts to concrete syntax
evidence_requirements: abstract, introduction, terminology, data model, and examples

patterns.title: Incubation and implementation signals
patterns.summary: Reviewers often check whether a proposal has adequate incubation, implementer interest, shipping pressure context, interoperability evidence, and unresolved design risk before standardization advances.
review_questions: What implementation or incubation evidence supports the design?
Is shipping pressure causing unresolved architectural questions to be skipped?
common_mitigations: separate blocking architectural issues from future work
evidence_requirements: explainer, implementation-status section, standards-position links, or review request context

patterns.title: Charter scope and deliverables
patterns.summary: Charter reviews should examine whether the proposed scope, deliverables, coordination plan, success criteria, and timeline are clear enough to expose architectural risk early.
review_questions: Are deliverables and non-goals concrete?
Are architectural dependencies and coordination groups identified?
Is the timeline plausible for the stated scope?
common_mitigations: separate exploratory work from normative deliverables
evidence_requirements: charter text, Strategy Funnel issue, AC review request, and deliverables section

patterns.title: Data minimization and purpose limitation
patterns.summary: The specification should limit data collection, exposure, and retention to what the stated purpose requires.
review_questions: What data is exposed, to whom, and for what purpose?
Can less precise or less persistent data satisfy the use case?
evidence_requirements: data model, privacy considerations, retention text

patterns.title: Sensitive and physical-world data
patterns.summary: Sensor, media, location, health, biometric, or physical-world signals can reveal people and environments beyond the immediate user.
review_questions: What physical-world data is exposed?
Can precision, sampling, or scope be reduced?

patterns.title: Stable identifiers and linkability
patterns.summary: Stable identifiers can allow correlation across sessions, origins, top-level sites, devices, or accounts.
review_questions: What boundary scopes the identifier?
Can it rotate or be pairwise?
Can users clear or revoke it?
common_mitigations: partition by top-level site and origin
evidence_requirements: identifier generation, scope, and lifetime rules

patterns.title: Fingerprinting and high-entropy surfaces
patterns.summary: Feature support, device properties, rendering behavior, errors, and timing can add entropy for browser or user fingerprinting.
review_questions: What new entropy does the feature expose?
Can values be rounded, bucketed, or permission-gated?
evidence_requirements: privacy considerations and exposed property definitions

patterns.title: Device enumeration
patterns.summary: Enumerating devices or local resources before user selection can reveal unique configuration and private context.
review_questions: Is full enumeration necessary?
Are labels hidden until permission or selection?

patterns.title: Persistent state, expiry, and clearability
patterns.summary: Persistent state should have clear lifetime, user clearing behavior, and interaction with private browsing or site-data controls.
review_questions: When does state expire?
How can users clear it?
Does clearing site data remove it?

patterns.title: Partitioning by site or origin
patterns.summary: Storage, identifiers, caches, permissions, and observations should be scoped to the right site or origin boundary.
review_questions: Is state partitioned by top-level site, origin, or another justified boundary?
common_mitigations: partition by top-level site and origin

patterns.title: First-party versus third-party access
patterns.summary: The specification should define whether and how embedded third parties can access data, capabilities, or observations.
review_questions: Can embedded contexts use the feature?
What top-level user or site control applies?
common_mitigations: deny by default in third parties

patterns.title: Permission transparency and revocation
patterns.summary: Users should understand, inspect, and revoke permissions or grants associated with sensitive data and capabilities.
review_questions: How is permission shown to users?
How can users revoke or inspect grants?

patterns.title: Private-browsing behavior
patterns.summary: Private or ephemeral browsing modes should not persist state or expose mode-specific fingerprinting unless explicitly justified.
review_questions: Does state persist in private browsing?
Can sites detect private mode through feature behavior?
evidence_requirements: private browsing or ephemeral mode behavior

patterns.title: Metadata leakage
patterns.summary: Headers, errors, timing, sizes, formats, and protocol metadata can reveal user, device, account, or browsing context.
review_questions: What metadata is observable to servers, intermediaries, or other origins?
Can it be minimized or partitioned?

patterns.title: Cross-context and cross-site correlation
patterns.summary: Signals available across windows, frames, workers, sites, or origins can correlate user activity.
review_questions: Which contexts can observe the signal?
Can cross-site correlation occur without user awareness?

patterns.title: Account enumeration
patterns.summary: Identity and credential flows should not let a site learn whether a user has an account or credential except through user-mediated disclosure.
review_questions: Can relying parties test account existence?
Are negative responses distinguishable before user mediation?

patterns.title: Location precision and background access
patterns.summary: Location-like or physical-world data should define precision, sampling, and background access limits.
review_questions: What precision is exposed?
Can access continue in the background?
Is approximate data sufficient?

patterns.title: Bystander privacy
patterns.summary: Media, sensors, and physical-world APIs can collect data about people who did not interact with the page.
review_questions: Can the feature capture bystanders?
Are indicators, minimization, or local processing available?
evidence_requirements: capture scope and user indicator behavior

patterns.title: Error oracles
patterns.summary: Differences in errors, timing, prompts, or rejection reasons can reveal account, permission, device, or state existence.
review_questions: Can callers distinguish private state through error detail or timing?

patterns.title: Network metadata and traffic correlation
patterns.summary: Network features can expose correlation signals through requests, redirects, cache state, headers, or timing.
review_questions: Can network observers or origins correlate browsing activity through this feature?
evidence_requirements: network request, redirect, and cache behavior

patterns.title: Privacy review package and considerations readiness
patterns.summary: Privacy reviewers need a stable review target, privacy considerations, self-review answers, known changes, and a clear issue venue before they can separate real privacy risk from missing review evidence.
review_questions: Does the request link to privacy considerations and self-review answers?
Are changes since prior review and the requested deadline clear?
common_mitigations: add privacy considerations and self-review links
identify the reviewed snapshot and changes
evidence_requirements: review request issue, privacy considerations, questionnaire answers, and transition context

patterns.title: Privacy risk in charter scope
patterns.summary: Charter reviews should check whether proposed deliverables or scope introduce personal-data, tracking, identity, profiling, or governance risks that need later privacy review.
review_questions: Do any deliverables create privacy-sensitive capabilities or data processing?
Does the charter route future privacy review to the right venue?
failure_modes: privacy-sensitive deliverable hidden in broad scope
common_mitigations: add privacy coordination or review milestones
evidence_requirements: charter scope, deliverables, coordination, and known-concerns sections

patterns.title: Secure-context gating
patterns.summary: Sensitive capabilities should be unavailable to insecure origins and fail closed on downgrade.
review_questions: Is access limited to secure contexts?
Does the feature fail closed if transport or context is insecure?

patterns.title: Powerful feature permission gating
patterns.summary: APIs that expose powerful features, sensitive data, or native capabilities should define an explicit permission model and integrate with platform permission mechanisms.
review_questions: Is this a powerful feature that needs an explicit permission gate?
Does the specification define Permissions API integration or another platform-consistent permission model?
What is the default permission state and fail-closed behavior before any grant?
Are permission checks performed before each sensitive operation and after revocation?
common_mitigations: integrate with Permissions API where applicable
recheck permission before acquisition or use
evidence_requirements: powerful-feature classification and permission processing model

patterns.title: Origin and site isolation
patterns.summary: Authority and observability should be scoped to origin or site boundaries with explicit cross-origin behavior.
review_questions: Which origin or site has authority?
Can one origin observe or affect another?

patterns.title: Capability delegation
patterns.summary: Delegating a capability to frames, workers, or services should require explicit authority and preserve least privilege.
review_questions: Who can delegate the capability?
Can the delegate exceed the delegator's authority?

patterns.title: Confused-deputy risks
patterns.summary: A more privileged browser, frame, identity provider, service worker, or native component should not be tricked into using authority for the wrong party.
review_questions: What principal is the feature acting for?
How is authority bound to the requester?

patterns.title: Trusted UI and spoofing
patterns.summary: Browser or native UI used for permission, identity, payment, or device selection should resist spoofing and clickjacking.
review_questions: Can web content spoof or obscure the UI?
Does the UI clearly identify the requesting origin and action?

patterns.title: Input validation
patterns.summary: Inputs from web content, network peers, files, devices, and native boundaries should be validated before use.
review_questions: What validation happens before processing?
Are malformed, oversized, or adversarial inputs defined?

patterns.title: Parser differential and canonicalization
patterns.summary: Formats and protocols should define canonical forms and parsing behavior to avoid inconsistent interpretation.
review_questions: Can two implementations parse the same bytes differently?
Is the signed or compared representation canonical?

patterns.title: Injection and unsafe URL handling
patterns.summary: Specifications that process URLs, strings, headers, markup, selectors, or commands should prevent injection into sensitive interpreters.
review_questions: Can untrusted input be interpreted as code, URL, header, or markup?
Are URL parsing and encoding rules explicit?
evidence_requirements: URL, string, and serialization processing rules

patterns.title: CSRF, replay, and origin binding
patterns.summary: Requests, assertions, credentials, and protocol messages should be bound to the intended origin, user action, freshness, and audience.
review_questions: Is the message bound to origin, audience, and freshness?
Can it be replayed or triggered cross-site?
common_mitigations: include origin and nonce in signed material

patterns.title: Authentication versus authorization
patterns.summary: The specification should distinguish proving identity from granting authority to act.
review_questions: What is being authenticated?
What authority is granted, by whom, and for how long?

patterns.title: Downgrade and fail-open behavior
patterns.summary: Features should not silently fall back to weaker security or privacy behavior when negotiation, support, or validation fails.
review_questions: What happens when stronger behavior is unavailable?
Can an attacker force weaker behavior?

patterns.title: Key lifecycle, randomness, and exportability
patterns.summary: Cryptographic designs should define key generation, storage, exportability, rotation, destruction, randomness, and algorithm constraints.
review_questions: How are keys generated, stored, exported, rotated, and destroyed?
What randomness requirements apply?

patterns.title: Resource exhaustion
patterns.summary: The feature should bound CPU, memory, storage, network, device, and UI resources under adversarial input or use.
review_questions: What resource limits apply?
Can attackers exhaust storage, CPU, network, or UI prompts?

patterns.title: Races and lifecycle transitions
patterns.summary: State changes across navigation, permission changes, worker shutdown, BFCache, or concurrent operations should avoid race vulnerabilities.
review_questions: What happens if authority changes during an operation?
Are state transitions atomic enough?

patterns.title: Cross-origin information leakage
patterns.summary: Cross-origin states should not leak through errors, timing, rendering, caches, redirects, or observable side effects.
review_questions: Can one origin infer another origin's state through the feature?

patterns.title: Malicious media or native-boundary input
patterns.summary: Media, device, and native-boundary inputs should be treated as adversarial and isolated from privileged components.
review_questions: What parser, decoder, or native component processes the input?
Is it sandboxed and validated?

patterns.title: Cache poisoning and integrity
patterns.summary: Caching and stored responses should preserve integrity, vary correctly, and avoid attacker-controlled cache confusion.
review_questions: What keys the cache?
Can attackers poison shared or partitioned cache entries?
Is integrity preserved?
common_mitigations: include origin and mode in cache key
evidence_requirements: cache key, storage, and integrity rules

patterns.title: Permission bypass
patterns.summary: No alternate entry point should bypass permission, user activation, policy, or origin checks.
review_questions: Are all entry points subject to the same permission and policy checks?
Can workers or iframes bypass UI gating?
common_mitigations: recheck permission on each entry point
evidence_requirements: permission checks for every entry point

patterns.title: Security review package and threat-readiness
patterns.summary: Security reviewers need a stable target, security considerations, known threat model or risk notes, changes since prior review, and a clear issue venue before they can assess controls.
review_questions: Does the request link to security considerations or threat analysis?
Are known security-sensitive changes and the issue venue clear?
common_mitigations: add security considerations and threat notes
identify the reviewed snapshot and changes
evidence_requirements: review request issue, security considerations, self-review or threat model, and transition context

patterns.title: Security risk in charter scope
patterns.summary: Charter reviews should check whether proposed deliverables or scope introduce authentication, authorization, network, cryptographic, browser-capability, or abuse risks that need later security review.
review_questions: Do any deliverables create security-sensitive capabilities or protocols?
Does the charter route future security review to the right venue?
failure_modes: security-sensitive deliverable hidden in broad scope
common_mitigations: add security coordination or review milestones
evidence_requirements: charter scope, deliverables, coordination, and known-risks sections
